design_summary.purpose: motor_control_top is the synthesizable ASIC digital IP top that wraps an external NVIDIA DoMINO automotive-aerodynamics service using a compact control-plane and transport-plane RTL wrapper. It provides a 64-bit software register window, bounded 128-bit outbound request and inbound response streaming interfaces, a 32-bit actuator command path, and top-level fault/busy/fallback status outputs. The RTL intentionally excludes the physics or surrogate model and instead implements request assembly, response qualification, timeout/watchdog handling, clamping and optional slew limiting, abort handling, sticky fault management, and safe-fallback behavior.
design_summary.operating_model: Software programs control/status registers, then asserts start_request while enable is set. The transport adapter assembles and issues a compact outbound metadata frame, waits for a bounded response, and exposes compact response fields to the validator. The validator checks sequence, type, age, and integrity qualifiers. Approved command metadata is post-processed by the limiter, which clamps to configured bounds and optionally limits slew before presenting act_cmd. The safety FSM coordinates the IDLE, ISSUE_REQUEST, WAIT_RESPONSE, VALIDATE_RESPONSE, APPLY_COMMAND, FALLBACK, and ABORT states, enforces single-outstanding ordering, latches faults, and drives busy_out and fallback_out.

module_architecture.name: motor_control_register_map
module_architecture.role: Register file and decode submodule for software control/status access.
responsibilities: Decode cfg_addr/cfg_we/cfg_re accesses into stable control registers.
Latch enable/start_request/abort/clear_fault and programmable scalar descriptors.
Provide readback of current configuration and safety/status fields.
Hold reset-safe defaults and expose deterministic read data for unmapped locations if required by architecture.
Present semantic outputs to top-level control logic without hidden derivation from the transport bus.
interface_notes: Consumes the 64-bit software register window and returns cfg_rdata/cfg_ready.

Produces semantic control outputs including enable, start_request, abort, clear_fault, model_id, request_seq, expected_response_seq, max_response_age, timeout_cycles, clamp_min, clamp_max, safe_fallback_cmd, request_flags, slew-limit enable, and slew-limit step.
Receives status inputs from the safety/control plane for software readback, including busy, fault, fallback, outstanding, last response OK, last error code, last actuator command, and last sequence.
Must remain limited to control/status storage and must not infer payload memories or bulk history banks.
ownership_notes: Owns the top-level software-visible register semantics.
Owns control decode and status readback mapping.
Does not own transport framing, response qualification, or actuator limiting.

module_architecture.name: motor_control_transport_adapter
module_architecture.role: Bounded transport-plane framing and capture adapter for the external runtime service.
responsibilities: Assemble tx_data from model ID, sequence, request type/flags, and scalar descriptors.
Assert tx_valid until tx_ready handshake completes.
Track outstanding request and sequence association.
Compute age/deadline status using cfg_timeout_cycles and/or cfg_max_response_age as designed.
Capture rx_data only when rx_valid and rx_ready are both asserted.
Extract compact response metadata for validation and command generation.
Support abort by canceling outstanding request context and returning to idle.
interface_notes: Drives outbound request valid/data and inbound response ready.
Consumes the software-programmed control fields that define the request descriptor.
Exposes request_outstanding, request_issued, request_seq_active, deadline_expired, request_age, and compact response summary signals.
Must remain single-outstanding and bounded, with no raw geometry payload storage or unbounded buffering.
ownership_notes: Owns request assembly and transport handshake behavior.
Owns request age/deadline tracking and compact response capture.
Does not own response acceptance policy or final actuator clamping.

module_architecture.name: motor_control_response_validator
module_architecture.role: Validation submodule that checks response sequence, response type, age, and integrity metadata.
responsibilities: Compare response sequence against request sequence and configured expectation.
Check response type and compact integrity metadata.
Gate approval on age/deadline status.
Emit a rejection code for status reporting.
Pass through only approved response command metadata to the command limiter/actuator path.
Remain purely synthesizable and side-effect free except for registered outputs.
interface_notes: Consumes compact response metadata from the transport adapter.
Produces response_accepted, response_rejected, rejection_code, approved_cmd_raw, approved_status, and approved_seq_match.
Rejects stale, duplicate, malformed, unexpected, or sequence-mismatched responses.
Approved outputs feed the command limiter and status readback path.
ownership_notes: Does not own clamp/slew logic or sticky fault policy directly.
Its rejection output is consumed by the safety FSM for fault latching.

module_architecture.name: motor_control_command_limiter
module_architecture.role: Command post-processing block that clamps approved actuator commands to configured bounds and optionally applies a bounded slew limit.
responsibilities: Select between approved command and safe fallback command.
Clamp to programmable min/max limits.
Optionally apply bounded slew limiting.
Assert act_valid when a new command is available for the actuator interface.
Hold act_valid until act_ready is observed, if required by implementation.
Provide registered limited and clamped command observability for status reporting.
interface_notes: Consumes approved command metadata plus safe fallback selection and clamp/slew configuration.
Produces act_valid, act_cmd, limited_cmd, clamped_cmd, and fallback_cmd_active.
Ensures the final command is bounded by clamp_min..clamp_max and optionally limited in step size.
Must not source commands from raw geometry or unvalidated data.
ownership_notes: Owns command selection between approved and fallback sources.
Owns clamp and optional slew-limit post-processing.
Does not own request generation, response rejection, or fault latching.

module_architecture.name: motor_control_safety_fsm
module_architecture.role: Safety and sequencing FSM that coordinates register decode, request issuance, response validation, command release, timeout handling, sticky fault management, software disable, and abort behavior.
responsibilities: Coordinate IDLE, ISSUE_REQUEST, WAIT_RESPONSE, VALIDATE_RESPONSE, APPLY_COMMAND, FALLBACK, and ABORT states.
Generate busy_out and fallback_out based on live transaction and safety state.
Latch and clear faults according to software policy.
Enforce enable/start_request/abort semantics.
Sequence and age validation must occur before command release.
Expose status readbacks for last error, last accepted sequence, and last actuator command.
interface_notes: Consumes enable/start_request/abort/clear_fault, timeout, request lifecycle status, response acceptance/rejection, deadline expiration, fallback command activity, and actuator acceptance.

Produces one-hot or equivalent state indicators, fault_latched, busy_out, fallback_out, status_last_error_code, status_request_outstanding, status_last_response_ok, status_last_seq, status_last_act_cmd, and command_applied.
Drives top-level fault_out, busy_out, and fallback_out through its state and sticky fault outputs.
Implements the explicit safety policy for software disable, abort, timeout, invalid response, and fault clearing.
ownership_notes: Owns the top-level safety state machine and sticky fault policy.
Owns the externally visible busy/fallback/fault indications.
Does not own register decode, transport framing, or response metadata extraction.

interface_summary.intent: Provide the semantic request configuration used to assemble and manage a bounded outbound request and its timeout/age tracking.
Provide the expected response sequence number for strict response qualification.
Provide command bounding and fallback parameters for the final actuator command path.
Provide software control bits and safety configuration to the FSM.
Expose the single-outstanding request context and compact inbound response metadata for validation.
Forward only approved compact command metadata to the command limiter.
Inform the safety FSM whether the response was approved or rejected so it can advance the state machine or latch fault/fallback.
Report whether the command path is currently sourcing the programmed safe fallback command.
Coordinate command application acceptance and fallback selection policy.
Return status, error, sequence, and command readbacks for software visibility.
Expose sticky fault, busy, and fallback status at the top-level pins.
Expose the 64-bit software register window read data and ready indication.
Expose the outbound request stream and inbound response backpressure control.
Expose the compact actuator command interface.

data_flow_summary: Software programs enable, start_request, abort, clear_fault, model_id, request_seq, expected_response_seq, max_response_age, timeout_cycles, clamp_min, clamp_max, safe_fallback_cmd, request_flags, and optional slew-limit parameters through the register map.
On an enabled start_request with no live transaction, the transport adapter assembles a compact 128-bit outbound metadata frame and holds tx_valid until tx_ready completes the handshake.
The transport adapter tracks request age and deadline expiration while awaiting a response, and it captures inbound rx_data only when rx_valid and rx_ready are both asserted.

The response validator compares the captured response against the active request sequence, expected response sequence, response type, age qualification, and integrity indication, then produces either approved metadata or a rejection code.

Approved response metadata flows into the command limiter, which selects between the approved command and the safe fallback command, clamps the result to clamp_min..clamp_max, and optionally applies bounded slew limiting.

The safety FSM observes request/response progress, deadline expiration, response rejection, software disable, and abort behavior, then drives busy_out, fallback_out, and sticky fault status accordingly.

The register map receives status feedback from the safety plane and command path so software can observe fault state, busy state, fallback state, outstanding transaction state, last response result, last error code, last sequence, and last actuator command.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: A single synchronous clock, clk, is distributed to the register map, transport adapter, response validator, command limiter, and safety FSM. The design is described as fully synthesizable with standard-cell logic and registered outputs where practical.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: The active-low reset_n initializes all control registers, counters, handshake qualifiers, state bits, and outputs to safe values. tx_valid deasserts, rx_ready is safely gated, act_valid deasserts, act_cmd returns to the safe fallback command if programmed or zero otherwise, busy_out deasserts, and fault_out clears. Any outstanding transaction context is canceled, and no stale response may be accepted until a new enabled start_request launches a fresh transaction.

integration_notes: The top module remains motor_control_top and must not be substituted by a register-bank, status-only, telemetry-only, or leaf module.

The top-level interface remains compact, bounded, and under the stated scalar-equivalent I/O limit, with no geometry arrays, point clouds, CFD fields, per-node outputs, or tensor buses at the top level.
The design is intentionally modular so transport framing, response validation, command limiting, and safety policy remain separable RTL blocks.

Single-outstanding transaction ordering is the baseline architecture; any future extension to multiple outstanding transactions would require only a compact sequence scoreboard, but that is outside the current contract.
No bulk payload storage is described here; only small control/status registers, counters, FSM state, and one-deep descriptor latches are part of the committed RTL behavior.

If future ASIC revisions require local bulk storage, the specified sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 hard macro is the only allowed memory macro, subject to complete verified collateral and a memory-collateral gate before use.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
